testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until you reach 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: The low air pressure warning signal should turn on when:
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the warning signal must turn on if air pressure drops below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system loses pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable change.
Lights on the vehicle will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one air system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop the vehicle safely and have the air system fixed.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the braking system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can let air out faster than the compressor can refill it.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may be slow to respond.
The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: If air pressure in an air brake system gets too low, the brakes will no longer work. This can happen if the brake pedal is pressed too many times without giving the compressor time to refill the air tanks.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and continue if they seem okay.
Drive with the hazard lights on.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on, stop and park the vehicle as soon as safely possible. You need to have some braking power left to stop safely.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, the rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. Air pressure enters when the driver:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes the rods out and moves the slack adjusters, which turn the brake camshafts.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, you should:
questions.explanation: To stop normally with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: The ____ shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: The air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping when air tank pressure reaches:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What stops wheels from locking up when you brake?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: What happens when brakes are not adjusted properly?

options.text: Some brakes work too hard and fail.
They help the vehicle accelerate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Some brakes work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check your brake adjustment often to avoid brake problems.

questions.question: When you must stop suddenly, what should you do?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle in a straight line.
Brake in a way that turns your vehicle.
Expect your vehicle to slow down faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle moving straight while braking. You should still be able to turn if needed.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system. The air compressor governor controls this process.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum safe air loss is 4 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are the tanks set up?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What color light shows that ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the ABS system is not working properly.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: In cold weather, check and fill the alcohol evaporator every day to prevent ice from building up in the air brake system.

questions.question: When is an alcohol evaporator most important?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator adds alcohol to the air brake system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: What must you do with a dual air brake system before driving?

options.text: The system keeps full air pressure when the vehicle is off.
The system keeps some air pressure when the vehicle is off.
You must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
You do not need time to build air pressure before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, run the engine until both the primary and secondary systems reach at least 100 psi.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. This means something is wrong and needs to be checked by a mechanic.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What should you do when making an emergency stop?

options.text: Turn the trailer to the right and stop.
Turn the trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. This method allows you to brake hard while still being able to steer if needed.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being used on the brakes. Not all air brake vehicles have this gauge.

questions.question: How does friction occur in an S-cam brake?

options.text: The brake shoes and linings press against the outside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum.
The brake shoes and linings push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when the brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.
